target_customer: Software engineering and platform teams running production services who need to find CPU and memory bottlenecks
problem: Profiling was usually a one-off, manual task done on a laptop or in a short production capture. Teams lacked an always-on, low-overhead way to see which lines of code burn CPU and memory over time.
business_model: Open source (AGPL) continuous profiling with a planned paid hosted and enterprise offering

founders.name: Dmitry Filimonov
founders.background_notes: Engineering team lead at Sensor Tower per the YC page.

founders.name: Ryan Perry
founders.background_notes: Software engineering, product and data engineering roles per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed low-overhead sampling profilers across several languages plus a compact storage and flame graph query engine. Hard parts were overhead and multi-language support, but it was standard engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Open source under AGPL with SDKs per language gave community and integration stickiness, but the core idea was copyable and well funded observability vendors could add profiling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Grafana built its own profiling database (Phlare) and then bought Pyroscope in March 2023 and merged the two into Grafana Pyroscope.

market_need_then: Observability was moving beyond metrics, logs and traces, and cloud cost pressure made code level CPU and memory waste visible. The project reached about 7.2k GitHub stars by the 2023 acquisition, per press coverage.

branding.domain_note: Used pyroscope.io, not the .com. The domain now redirects to Grafana docs.

rebrands.why: Grafana merged the two projects after the acquisition and kept the Pyroscope name.

branding.community_and_virality: Open source community with about 7.2k GitHub stars by March 2023 and a Grafana plugin integration since mid 2021, per coverage.

brand_strength.rationale: The name survived the acquisition as the product name inside Grafana, which shows it had recognition among developers, but no sources show merch, mascot or press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Pyroscope grew an open source continuous profiling project to about 7.2k GitHub stars and a Grafana integration within two years of the W21 batch. Grafana had built a competing database called Phlare, and in March 2023 it acquired the company and merged the projects under the Pyroscope name, a strategic acquisition with undisclosed terms.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators show about $125K to $130K seed in 2021 (CB Insights and similar), another aggregator shows $80M which is implausible. None recorded as rounds. Competition search found no sources dated near early 2021 so the competitor list is empty; Parca open sourced in late 2021 per a comparison article and Google Cloud Profiler and Datadog profiler existed earlier but no dated sources were found. Company website pyroscope.io redirects to Grafana docs. Completeness pass: a 2021 seed round is recorded from TechCrunch (seed in 2021) with investors from CB Insights (single database, led by General Catalyst); amount left null because CB Insights shows about 130K across four rounds, Extruct shows an implausible 80M, and a 2.5M figure is only a founder goal quote. Acquired by Grafana Labs in March 2023.
